HMW-V25: Vendor Period Billing Summary

How might we let vendor operators see their total billable amount across all verified jobs — so they know when and how much to invoice Teleport, without counting manually or leaving the app?
Root cause: The vendor app shows fees per-job in the detail page, but no aggregation exists. A vendor finance admin reconciling November 2026 must open each of their 14–20 verified jobs, note the fee total, and sum them in a spreadsheet. The "Verified" segment in My Jobs already filters to billing-ready jobs — it's the natural place to surface this total. The two-signal model means Verified = admin sign-off complete = safe to invoice. The gap: nothing bridges the per-job fee table and the monthly invoice.

Context: HaleSun Logistics has 14 verified jobs in November 2026. 11 are CNY-denominated (customs clearance, handling), 3 are USD (ocean freight components). Their finance admin opens Teleport OS vendor app at month-end to compile the invoice. Currently: she screenshots each job's fee section and pastes into Excel.

Option A — Verification Stats Strip (zero new screen real estate)

Option A
A 28px green-tinted strip appears above the job table only when the Verified segment is active. It shows the total verified amounts per currency, job count, and the implicit period (all verified jobs in the current filter). The strip vanishes when the user switches to any other segment. No new page, no new nav item, no structural change.

Pros:
· Zero new navigation or page surface
· Appears exactly where and when it's relevant (Verified segment)
· Respects the dense-data principle: strip is 28px
· Automatically scoped to current filters (service, date)
· "Last verified" timestamp tells vendor when to expect no more additions
Cons:
· No trip-level breakdown (vendor can't see which trip contributed what)
· No download/copy action on the total — still requires manual invoice writing
· Multi-currency side-by-side may be confusing if jobs have mixed currencies
· "Amount" column requires a new column in the job table (currently 7 columns)

Option B — Billing Summary Panel (below table, Verified segment only)

Option B
A collapsible "Billing Summary" panel appears below the job table in the Verified segment. It groups verified jobs by trip + customer, shows per-currency subtotals per trip, and a grand total at the bottom. Collapsed by default; vendor expands when they need a breakdown. Deeper than the strip but no new nav.

Pros:
· Trip-level breakdown answers "which trip contributed what?" (useful for per-trip invoices)
· Grand total per currency directly writable on an invoice
· Collapsible — doesn't take up space when not needed
· No new nav or page required
· "Based on Teleport-verified amounts" framing prevents disputes
Cons:
· Pushes the panel below the fold — vendor must scroll past 14+ job rows
· No copy/export action from the panel itself
· Period is implicit (all verified jobs) — no month selector for multi-period cleanup
· Requires knowing to scroll down; not visible at page load

Option C — Dedicated Billing Page (new nav item)

Option C
A third nav item "Billing" (My Jobs | Fleet | Billing) with a dedicated period selector. Vendors pick a month, see the breakdown by trip + customer, and get a grand total per currency. Includes a "Copy invoice total" action. Useful for finance admins, but adds permanent nav complexity for ops dispatchers who never use it.

Pros:
· Period selector handles multi-month cleanup (vendor paid for Oct but Oct still shows in Verified)
· "Copy total" action closes the last-mile invoice gap without an external spreadsheet
· Dedicated page doesn't pollute the ops dispatcher's My Jobs view
· Finance admin and ops dispatcher can use different nav items for their role
Cons:
· Third nav item adds permanent complexity for vendors who never need billing summary
· "Billing" page may imply invoicing features that aren't there (creates expectation)
· Duplicates the job list table in a new context
· Stat cards (3-up) are closer to AI slop than the dense-data principle; would need careful treatment
· Wrong for v1 — billing reporting is a v2 concern when vendor count scales

Recommendation: Option A for v1 + Option B for v1.1

v1 — Verification Stats Strip (Option A): Ship the billing strip above the job table when the Verified segment is active. Add an "Amount" column to the job table (rightmost, text-right, JetBrains Mono). The strip aggregates that column per currency. This is the minimal viable answer to "how much am I owed?" — it appears where the vendor is already standing (Verified segment), costs one new column and one new 28px strip, and respects the dense-data principle.

v1.1 — Billing Summary Panel (Option B): When vendors start asking "which trip is this for?" (which they will, once they invoice Teleport per-trip), add the collapsible panel below the table. Trip-level grouping lets them match the Teleport total to their own internal per-trip cost tracking. The panel should include a "Copy totals" button that copies a plain-text invoice memo (Chinese labels: 客户/航次/金额) to the clipboard for WeChat forwarding to Teleport's finance team.

Option C deferred to v2: When Teleport has 10+ active vendors and vendors need month-end reporting with period selection, add the Billing page. For v1, dispatchers and finance admins use the same view — the strip satisfies both.

Open questions: (1) Should the "Amount" column in the job table show the fee total from that job's Fee Breakdown, or the billing-confirmed amount? Recommend: Fee Breakdown total (read from job fees), since that's the number on the invoice. (2) Should the stats strip also show a forecast row for "Completed but not yet Verified" (amber, muted)? Recommend: yes, as a secondary line in the strip — it answers "what's coming next month?" without cluttering the verified total.
